editorial:
Imagine walking into a police station for help, but the only person who can speak your language is the one lying for you. That is the nightmare you see in this movie. You follow a mother in a burqa who just wants to protect her son from her mean husband. She thinks she is finally safe because she is talking to the law, but the translator is actually twisting her words to make her sound crazy or confused. The vibe is super tense because you can see the truth, but the police officers are totally blind to it. It makes you feel frustrated and worried for her in a way that keeps you glued to the screen.

The acting is what really sells this story. You do not need a lot of dialogue to feel the pain and fear on the mother's face. While the movie is slow and focuses on one room, the tension builds up like a ticking bomb. If you like stories about social issues and strong female leads, you will love this.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a heartbreaking note. Despite her best efforts to tell the truth, the translator successfully tricks the police into believing the husband's version of the story. The mother realizes that the system is not there to save her because of the language barrier and bias. She is forced to leave the station without any real help, leaving her and her son trapped in a scary situation with no way out.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful stories about human rights and overcoming odds.
